headline: Sensex tumbles 600 points and Nifty slips below 23,000 amid weak global cues and rising oil prices

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Weak signals from Asian markets including Nikkei and Kospi weighed on domestic sentiment
Rising crude oil prices and concerns over inflation triggered a sharp market dip
Continued FPI outflows from Indian equities have impacted market liquidity
GIFT Nifty indicated a weak opening, trading down by 0.52% before the session
whatHappening: The Sensex tumbled over 600 points while the NSE Nifty50 opened below the 23,000 mark
Markets hit a three-month low following the longest weekly losing streak since 2020
MCX revenue is projected to grow 19% annually through FY30 due to a wider investor base
Augment India is likely to sell a stake worth Rs 1,063 crore in Clean Max through a block deal
summary: The Indian stock market opened sharply lower on September 28, with the Sensex falling over 600 points and Nifty dropping below 23,000. Negative global cues, rising oil prices, and sustained FPI outflows are the primary drivers of the current downturn. Despite the broad sell-off, specific stocks like MCX and Cyient are seeing interest due to positive growth forecasts and technical patterns.
